periods.analysis: We are opening the K-3 Literacy Acceleration Initiative at 10% complete and green, which is the right starting posture: disciplined, staffed, and already visible in classrooms. The two foundation moves are complete—reading coaches are hired at all 12 Title-I schools, and every K-3 schedule now protects a daily intervention block rather than treating reading support as optional enrichment. Coaches began common lesson-study rounds on the Bayline, East Harbor, and Southport feeder patterns, with early focus on phonemic awareness routines and decodable-text use. The mid-year FAST progress-monitoring review is in progress and due in 20 days, while the summer bridge program for retained 3rd-graders remains not started with 120 days to build it correctly.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green status by keeping the 12 coaches in schools four days per week and reserving Fridays for data review, model lessons, and calibration with principals. I recommend we lock the summer bridge site list, transportation assumptions, and teacher stipends now, not after retention decisions become emotional and rushed. Attendance is the watch-item: principals should flag any K-3 student missing two intervention blocks in a month for same-week family outreach.

periods.analysis: The initiative moved from 10% to 15% complete, a 5-point quarter-over-quarter gain, and remains green because implementation is growing without losing the instructional core. The completed coach hiring and daily K-3 intervention blocks are holding steady across the 12 Title-I schools, and walk-throughs show the strongest fidelity at Carver, Marina Park, and North Jetty Elementary. The FAST progress-monitoring review is still in progress with the 20-day due point in view, giving us a clean window to compare intervention groups before winter schedule changes. Summer bridge is still not started and remains 120 days out, which is acceptable only if we keep the design work moving now.
periods.recommendations: Continue the protected intervention block and require each school to submit one revised small-group roster after FAST data meetings, using no more than six students per intensive group where staffing allows. Extend the coach model by pairing the three highest-fidelity campuses with three campuses needing tighter routines for January peer observations. Begin drafting the summer bridge scope of work, including curriculum kits, breakfast service, and airport-area bus Route SB-3 coverage for Southport families.

periods.analysis: We are now at 20% complete, up another 5 points quarter over quarter from 15%, and the initiative remains green. The work is shifting from installation to quality: coaches are no longer just helping teachers find materials; they are coaching error correction, fluency timing, and comprehension checks inside the daily K-3 intervention block. The mid-year FAST progress-monitoring review remains in progress and due in 20 days, and the assessment team has loaded class-level files into the Harborview Literacy Tracker for principal conferences. Summer bridge for retained 3rd-graders is still not started with 120 days remaining, but we now have enough student-level risk information to design it around real need rather than averages.
periods.recommendations: Sustain momentum by holding principal data conferences within five school days of the FAST review and documenting one action per grade level in the Literacy Tracker. Extend intervention quality by having coaches complete two side-by-side model lessons per month in classrooms where chronic absenteeism is weakening dosage. Move summer bridge from concept to operating plan by naming site leads, confirming the adopted reading curriculum sequence, and pre-clearing HR pools for certified teachers.

periods.analysis: The initiative reached 25% complete, a 5-point increase from 20%, and it remains green heading into the season when literacy gains can either compound or leak away. The 12 Title-I reading coaches are embedded enough now to identify pattern problems—especially blending accuracy in grade 1 and multisyllabic decoding in grade 3—rather than treating every classroom as a blank slate. The daily intervention block remains complete and active, including the port-neighborhood schools where family work schedules can complicate attendance. The FAST progress-monitoring review is still in progress with the 20-day due marker, and summer bridge remains not started at 120 days out, which makes operational readiness the next test.
periods.recommendations: Keep the intervention block intact through end-of-year events; assemblies, testing logistics, and field days should not consume the one protected literacy period. I recommend launching summer bridge enrollment packets now for likely retained 3rd-graders, with translated family calls from the Seabreeze and Harbor Heights community liaisons. Extend the green result by contracting buses for two north-south routes and one crosstown route before vendor capacity tightens for summer camps.

periods.analysis: At 30% complete, up 5 points quarter over quarter from 25%, the initiative is still green and beginning to show the habits of a system rather than a pilot. The completed coach hiring and daily intervention block have become normal operating procedure in the 12 Title-I schools, which is exactly how early literacy work should feel: consistent, visible, and boring in the best sense. Coach logs from Bayside, Juniper, and West Canal show more teachers using quick mastery checks before regrouping students, a sign that the work is moving from compliance to judgment. The FAST review remains in progress and due in 20 days, while summer bridge is still not started with 120 days remaining, so we should treat planning discipline as the risk-control lever.
periods.recommendations: Sustain implementation by publishing a monthly K-3 intervention fidelity dashboard for principals, coaches, and area supervisors, using walk-through evidence rather than anecdotes. Extend the strongest practice by creating a three-school demonstration loop where teachers observe a full intervention block from entry routine to exit ticket. For summer bridge, finalize the retained 3rd-grade student identification protocol and make sure no school is waiting for perfect data before beginning family engagement.

periods.analysis: The initiative advanced to 35% complete, another 5-point quarter-over-quarter gain from 30%, and it remains green with a more mature implementation base. I am encouraged that the 12 Title-I coaches are now leading grade-level data talks instead of only responding to individual teacher requests, because that is how we build capacity that survives staff turnover. The daily K-3 intervention block continues to be the anchor, and Harborview’s growth pressures have not displaced it even in crowded campuses near the airport corridor. The mid-year FAST progress-monitoring review is still in progress and due in 20 days, and the summer bridge program remains not started at 120 days out, keeping urgency on design and logistics.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the green trajectory by protecting coach caseloads from unrelated duties during testing season and documenting any principal-approved exception. Extend the model by training assistant principals to lead 20-minute literacy data huddles, so the work is not dependent on a single coach in each building. I recommend completing the summer bridge staffing matrix now, including teacher, paraprofessional, nurse, food service, and bus monitor coverage by site.

periods.analysis: We are at 40% complete, up 5 points from 35% last quarter, and the initiative remains green because the implementation architecture is stable. The completed milestones—12 Title-I reading coaches hired and daily K-3 intervention blocks added—are no longer launch tasks; they are the operating floor for how Harborview teaches early reading. The FAST progress-monitoring review remains in progress with 20 days to the due point, and school teams are using the current cycle to distinguish students who need more time from students who need a different intervention. Summer bridge for retained 3rd-graders is still not started with 120 days remaining, and that is the one area where I want planning to move faster before spring calendars crowd us.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the core by requiring every Title-I principal to observe one K-3 intervention block weekly and give written feedback tied to grouping, pacing, and student response. Extend impact by adding a Saturday family literacy lab at four hub schools—Carver, East Harbor, Marina Park, and Southport—focused on take-home decodable practice and attendance recovery. Move summer bridge into procurement by ordering instructional materials, confirming meal service counts, and reserving classrooms before maintenance schedules are finalized.

periods.analysis: The initiative closes this sequence at 45% complete, a 5-point quarter-over-quarter increase from 40%, and it remains green with clear evidence of sustained execution. Across the arc from 10% in 2024-Q3 to 45% now, Harborview has done the unglamorous work well: hire the 12 Title-I reading coaches, protect the daily K-3 intervention block, and keep data conversations focused on children rather than excuses. The FAST progress-monitoring review remains in progress and due in 20 days, so the next round of decisions should be made from fresh evidence, not from spring impressions. Summer bridge is still not started with 120 days remaining, and that makes it the next operational gate for preserving gains among retained 3rd-graders.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green result by making the coach-plus-intervention-block model part of next year’s school improvement plans and budget assumptions, not a temporary initiative line. Extend the work by adding a small central literacy response team to cover vacancies, new-teacher classrooms, and schools with high chronic absenteeism before students lose intervention dosage. I recommend setting a 30-day deadline to launch summer bridge operations: sites confirmed, families notified, rosters drafted, staff hired, and transportation routes tested.

periods.analysis: 75% complete. 0 of 4 milestones are done. Next up: Reading coaches hired at 12 Title-I schools (due Feb 16, 2026).
periods.recommendations: Review the late milestones with the project owner and confirm recovery dates before the next reporting cycle.
